homePage.healthDataOperational: HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform fully operational (as per EHDS Regulation)
homePage.overview_description_part_1: Release 4 represents a key milestone in the development of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Infrastructure. It introduces major functional enhancements, including full multilingual support across all official EU languages, the first version of the Data Permit feature, and a new Documentation page providing practical guidance and technical resources.
homePage.overview_description_part_2: This release also brings improvements to the Dataset Catalogue, strengthens machine-to-machine interoperability between the Central Platform and National Contact Points, and enhances the platform’s resilience and security. Together, these updates contribute to a more robust, user-friendly, and transparent infrastructure for the secondary use of health data in the EU.
homePage.open_source_description: The solutions for both the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Infrastructure are now available as open-source software as Commission aims to promote transparency and enable wider adoption by stakeholders across Europe. These solutions are available under a license and can be accessed on code.europa.eu.
homePage.central_platform_description: The HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform is a pivotal digital system being developed by the European Commission to meet the requirements of the upcoming European Health Data Space Regulation. This platform hosts the Dataset Catalogue, which compiles metadata from member states, European institutions, third countries, and research infrastructures. Additionally, the key functionalities include completing and submitting Data Access and Data Request applications for assessment and decision-making by relevant Health Data Access Bodies.
homePage.infrastructure_description: Release 3 enables creation, updates, and deletion operations on the Dataset Catalogue via a secure machine-to-machine connection between the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Contact Points. These Contact Points include entities from member states, European institutions, third countries, and research infrastructures. The connection leverages the eDelivery AS4 software infrastructure, ensuring a robust and secure system developed and tested by the European Commission in collaboration with the EHDS2 Pilot project.
homePage.key_features_release_4_description: Release 4 includes several new features to enhance the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Infrastructure:

release_4_features.title: Multilingual User Interface
release_4_features.description: The platform is now available in all official EU languages, as well as Norwegian (Bokmål and Nynorsk) and Icelandic. This applies to all static interface elements (excluding metadata content).

release_4_features.title: Data Permit Decision
release_4_features.description: Users can observe the proposal for the Application details and Data Permit feature and provide comments directly for future implementation.

release_4_features.title: New Documentation Page
release_4_features.description: A dedicated section now provides guidance and information on regulatory compliance, platform functionalities, onboarding for new users, open-source resources, and other helpful links for the community.

release_4_features.title: Administration Panel (Back-Office)
release_4_features.description: Users with administrator rights can now access real-time audit logs, user and dataset catalogue management tools through a dedicated panel.

release_4_features.title: Back-End Self-Testing
release_4_features.description: The system now includes self-testing capabilities, making deployments more robust and reducing the risk of regression.

release_4_features.title: Autonomous Testing for Member States
release_4_features.description: Development teams from Member States can use an intuitive testing platform integrated in the Interoperability Test Bed. It supports onboarding, connectivity and functional testing with full conformance to the platform’s messaging standards.

release_4_features.title: Enhanced Security and Quality Assurance
release_4_features.description: This release includes an updated user interface, regular vulnerability mitigation, and a clean Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) to ensure traceability and transparency.

homePage.releaseOpenForTesting: This release is open for community testing and feedback.
homePage.memberStatesRepresentativesInvited: Users and Member States representatives are warmly invited to explore the new features, test the multilingual interface, interact with the Data Permit prototype, and consult the new documentation. Your input is essential to refine and finalize future developments.

release_3_features.title: Updated cross-border gateway (eDelivery)
release_3_features.description: The revised solution for HealthData{'@'}EU Infrastructure based on the eDelivery AS4 can now be used by both the Central Platform and all Contact Points to establish trusted and secure connections.

release_3_features.title: Data Request Application Management
release_3_features.description: Users can display, complete, modify, and submit Data Request applications through an improved user interface.

release_3_features.title: Data Application Export
release_3_features.description: Users can export applications in a human-readable format for offline review or sharing.

release_3_features.title: Application Status History
release_3_features.description: Users can view the history of actions taken on their applications for better tracking and transparency.

release_3_features.title: Improved Navigation
release_3_features.description: Users can consult detailed descriptions of preliminary version of HealthDCAT-AP elements, improving navigation and search functionality within the Dataset Catalogue.

release_2_features.title: User Identification and Authentication
release_2_features.description: Users can now log in using their EU login credentials, ensuring secure and clear identification.

release_2_features.title: User Authorization
release_2_features.description: A new feature allows the creation of different user roles, with easy tools to manage and update user access.

release_2_features.title: Data Permit Application Status
release_2_features.description: The system now supports better tracking and management of application statuses between Contact Points and the Dataset Catalogue.

release_2_features.title: Health DCAT-AP Validation according to the constraint file
release_2_features.description: This service checks that all incoming datasets meet the Health DCAT-AP standard, ensuring consistency and accuracy.

release_1_features.title: Search and Display
release_1_features.description: Explore the Dataset Catalogue, which follows the first release of the Health DCAT-AP standard.

release_1_features.title: Data Permit Applications
release_1_features.description: Manage Data Access applications by displaying, completing, modifying, and submitting forms.

quality.dcatApCompliance:
DCAT-AP compliance is calculated across all sources and dataset records available on a catalogue. This check is only performed if the metadata is originally harvested as DCAT-AP or as a valid derivate.

DCAT-AP is a specification for describing linked public data in Europe. The data.europe.eu portal may also harvest metadata which does not fully comply to DCAT-AP. In order to increase conformity to DCAT-AP, the MQA checks each metadata for its DCAT-AP compliance.

The metadata is validated against a set of SHACL shapes. The metadata is not compliant, if the SHACL validation reports at least one issue.

The MQA uses data.europe.eu's DCAT-AP SHACL validation sevice.

SCHACL is a recommendation from the W3C and is used for validating RDF graphs against a set of shapes.

context.paragraph1: The Dataset Description Assistant (DDA) is a user interface designed to assist data holders in creating structured dataset descriptions aligned with the {spec}. It provides a dynamic, user-friendly form that promotes metadata quality, consistency, and compliance, while adapting to the dataset’s Access Rights.
context.paragraph2: Users can select one of three access levels: Non-public, Restricted, or Public. Based on the selected access right, the Assistant dynamically enforces the appropriate HealthDCAT-AP rules, automatically adjusting the properties and fields displayed within the form.
context.paragraph3: By default, the DDA saves form content only for the current session. However, authenticated users have the ability to save their progress to their profile and further refine their exported metadata file by validating it through the HealthData{'@'}EU Validator.

metadataModelExplorer.title: Metadata Model Explorer

context.title: Context
context.paragraph1: The HealthDCAT-AP Metadata Model Explorer is an implementation support tool designed to help users apply the {spec}. It presents, through a user-friendly interface, the metadata elements used to describe datasets intended for secondary use of electronic health data in the European Union. For each element, it displays definitions, cardinalities, usage notes and RDF examples, enabling consistent implementation across Member States.
context.paragraph2: HealthDCAT-AP is a domain-specific extension of the DCAT Application Profile for data portals in Europe (DCAT-AP), tailored to the needs of the European Health Data Space (EHDS) established by Regulation (EU) 2025/327. It provides a common semantic model for describing health datasets in a structured and machine-readable way. This supports the implementation of Article 77 of the EHDS Regulation, which requires the creation of a common EU dataset catalogue.
context.paragraph3: By facilitating the harmonised application of metadata, HealthDCAT-AP enhances the findability, transparency and legal certainty of dataset descriptions. It contributes to the semantic and technical interoperability of the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure and supports the enforcement of common rules on access and reuse conditions.
context.paragraph4: HealthDCAT-AP was initially designed under the EHDS2 Pilot Project, and further refined in the context of the TEHDAS2 Joint Action. Its governance, ongoing evolution and maintenance are now under the responsibility of the European Commission, in close cooperation with Member States and relevant stakeholders. All updates are published transparently through a dedicated open-source repository.
context.paragraph5: This work contributes to the broader objectives of the European strategy for data, which aims to establish Common European Data Spaces in strategic sectors. In this context, HealthDCAT-AP provides the semantic foundation of the health data space, enabling secure, cross-border data reuse for research, innovation, public health, policy-making and regulatory purposes.
context.paragraph6: This version of the Explorer is aligned with the technical architecture of the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure. It is also intended to support future updates and facilitate implementation through practical guidance.

helpIcon.scoring: data.europa.eu measures the quality of all dataset records and services. In the Data/Metadata Quality section we have a methodology page that describes the process. Each dataset record and service is also represented by a quality score. This score can be sufficient, good or excellent. If the filter "Sufficient+" is set, all dataset records and services that have a sufficient score or better would be shown. The same applies for "Good". "Excellent" only shows excellent dataset records and services.
helpIcon.license: A licence describes the legal conditions on how a dataset record can be used.
helpIcon.dataScope: Geographical or organizational scope of the dataset, e.g., EU, international, or national data.
helpIcon.format: File type or service type used to represent the dataset, such as CSV or JSON.
helpIcon.catalog: Repository or portal hosting the dataset and its associated data services.
helpIcon.settings: Decide whether your filter selection is exclusive or not. If you select AND all the search results must match all filters. OR means that at least one filter has to match.
helpIcon.categories: A theme groups dataset records sharing a common topic.
helpIcon.publisher: A publisher is a type of organisation that makes the dataset available.
helpIcon.keywords: Descriptive terms that help identify the dataset's content for search and discovery.
helpIcon.age_range: Typical age range of the population within the dataset.
helpIcon.hdab: Authority in charge of granting access to health data in compliance the EHDS regulation.
helpIcon.custodian: Agent responsible for making the health data resource available.
helpIcon.health_category: Standardized set of terms that defines the specific categories of electronic health data as outlined in Article 51 of the EHDS Regulation proposal
helpIcon.health_theme: Label or category that describes the main subject or topic of a dataset, specifically related to health, it works as a tag to help organize datasets, making it easier to find and group together datasets on similar health topics, e.g.:  home nursing, inpatient care, medical diagnosis, viral vaccines.
helpIcon.has_coding_system:
1.    Classification system used for health data coding, e.g., ICD-10, DRGs, SNOMED CT, OMOP
2.    Inside the filter there is a tooltip for each code with the wikidata description.
helpIcon.conforms_to: Refers to interoperability standard, implementation rules, or other specification that the health data conforms to. e.g.: HL7 FHIR, HL7v2, HL7 CDA, openEHR, IHE, CEN.
helpIcon.number_of_unique_individuals: Number of records for unique individuals.
helpIcon.accrual_periodicity: The frequency at which the Dataset is updated.
helpIcon.has_personal_data: Key elements that represent an individual in the dataset.
helpIcon.has_code_values: Health classifications and their codes associated with the dataset.
helpIcon.type: Indicates quality and utility of the dataset.
helpIcon.country: A geographic region that is covered by the Dataset.
helpIcon.access_right: Defines whether access to the dataset is public, restricted, or non-public.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.description: Glossary of terms used in health data applications

applicant.title: Applicant
applicant.content: The person applying for data, the data user (if access is granted).

controller.title: Controller
controller.content: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others (‘joint controllership’), determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data; where the purposes and means of such processing are determined by Union or Member State law, the controller or the specific criteria for its nomination may be provided for by Union or Member State law.

dataAccessApplication.title: Data Access Application
dataAccessApplication.content: An application seeking to access personal level electronic health data for secondary use in an anonymised or a pseudonymised format.

dataExtractionDescription.title: Data Extraction Description
dataExtractionDescription.content: A document outlining which data are applied for specifying the geographical location(s), register(s), dataset record(s) and variable(s). An attachment that must be filled in and attached to the data access application form.

dataHolder.title: Data Holder
dataHolder.content: A person, an entity or a body registering and storing health data. The data holder makes electronic health data available as per the EHDS Regulation. It also communicates to the Health Data Access Body a general description of the Dataset Record it holds.

dataRegistry.title: Data Registry
dataRegistry.content: A collection of data. Data registry is managed by an authority or an organisation.

dataRequest.title: Data Request Application
dataRequest.content: An application for accessing electronic health data for secondary use in an anonymised statistical format.

dataUser.title: Data User
dataUser.content: A natural or a legal person who has lawful access to personal or non-personal electronic health data for secondary use.

extractionMethod.title: Extraction Method
extractionMethod.content: A way of retrieving data. For example, retrieving a random sample of a defined group of data subjects, retrieving all the data subjects fulfilling a defined set of criteria, or another method.

general.title: General Data Protection Regulation
general.content: It sets out detailed requirements for companies and organisations on collecting, storing and managing personal data. It applies both to European organisations that process personal data of individuals in the EU, and to organisations outside the EU that target people living in the EU. Acronym: GDPR.

health.title: Health Data Access Body
health.content: Bodies that are responsible for processing the health data applications and granting access to electronic health data for secondary use if the application is accepted. Acronym: HDAB.

regulation.title: Regulation on the European Health Data Space (EHDS)
regulation.content: A legal document establishing the framework and rules regarding the creation and functioning of a common space where natural persons can easily control their electronic health data. It will also enable researchers, innovators and policy makers to use this electronic health data in a trusted and secure way that preserves privacy.

studyCohort.title: Study Cohort
studyCohort.content: The group of people whose data are studied. Also known as ‘study population’ or ‘group of data subjects’.

availability.title: Availability of data in different EU countries
availability.content:
The availability of data for secondary use varies across Member States in terms of scope, content, data quality, and level of aggregation.
Each Health Data Access Body (HDAB) manages the datasets under its remit, while the EU Dataset Catalogue (established under Article 77 of the EHDS Regulation) provides a single-entry point to explore available datasets and metadata across the EU.
Users can browse the available datasets and metadata through the EU Dataset Catalogue to identify where relevant data exist and which HDABs manage them.

allowedProhibitedPurposes.title: Allowed Purposes for Secondary Use of Health Data
allowedProhibitedPurposes.intro: Access to electronic health data under the EHDS Regulation can only be authorised for purposes that serve the public interest and generate benefits for health, society, or innovation (Article 53).
allowedProhibitedPurposes.publicHealth: Public health – monitoring, preventing, or responding to health threats; ensuring quality and safety of healthcare.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.publicHealthExample: Example: monitoring vaccination coverage or disease prevalence to guide prevention measures.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.supportBodies: Support to public bodies – providing evidence to national or EU authorities for policymaking, resource allocation or health system planning.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.supportBodiesExample: Example: analysing hospital admissions to support preparedness planning.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.statistics: Statistics – producing official or research-based health statistics and indicators.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.statisticsExample: Example: generating EU-wide statistics on chronic disease prevalence.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.education: Education and training – using anonymised data for teaching or academic purposes in health and care sectors.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.educationExample: Example: developing training material for medical students.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.research: Scientific research and innovation – conducting studies to improve prevention, diagnosis, or treatment, or to develop new medicinal products, devices, or digital health solutions.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.researchExample: Example: using pseudonymised data to study genetic markers of rare diseases.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.ai: Algorithm and AI testing – training, validating or evaluating algorithms, AI systems or other analytical tools in health.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.aiExample: Example: validating an AI model that detects early signs of heart disease.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.improvingCare: Improving healthcare delivery – evaluating and optimising healthcare pathways, treatment outcomes or system performance based on health data.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.improvingCareExample: Example: assessing effectiveness of chronic disease management programmes.
allowedProhibitedPurposes.closing: These purposes should be pursued in the interest of the public and not for individual or commercial advantage.

prohibitedPurposes.title: Prohibited Purposes for Secondary Use of Health Data
prohibitedPurposes.intro: Under Article 54 of the EHDS Regulation, access to health data cannot be granted for purposes that may harm individuals, groups or society.
prohibitedPurposes.heading: Prohibited uses include:

items.decisions: making decisions detrimental to individuals or groups based on their health data (e.g. employment, credit, or eligibility decisions);
items.insurance: insurance discrimination, such as modifying premiums or excluding benefits;
items.marketing: advertising or marketing to health professionals or the public using health data;
items.disclosure: unauthorised disclosure or sharing of health data with third parties not covered by the data permit;
items.harmfulProducts: development of harmful or unethical products or services, such as those that promote addiction or contravene public order and morality.

prohibitedPurposes.responsibility: All data users are responsible for ensuring that their projects strictly comply with these conditions.
prohibitedPurposes.guidelineText: For detailed legal explanations and examples, consult the official TEHDAS2 guideline: Deliverable 5.2 – Allowed and Prohibited Purposes {ref}.

penaltiesForMisuseOfElectronicData.title: Penalties for misuse of electronic health data
penaltiesForMisuseOfElectronicData.p1_before: Health Data Access Bodies (HDABs) are responsible for

penaltiesForMisuseOfElectronicData.p2: If a data user or holder violates the conditions of a data permit or uses data for unauthorised purposes, the HDAB may:

items.suspendRevoke: suspend or revoke the data permit;
items.terminate: terminate the ongoing data processing operation;

whatDocumentsAndInformation.intro_emphasis: data request or data access application
whatDocumentsAndInformation.intro_after: , prepare the following information and documents to ensure a smooth and efficient process:

items.publicSummary_text: (Article 58): a short, non-confidential abstract that can be published by the HDAB once the permit or reply is issued.
items.projectPlan_text: : a concise description (max 2 pages) of objectives, methodology and expected outcomes.
items.dataNeeds_text: : specify datasets required, timeframes, variables and data categories.

items.ethics_text: : where required by national law or the data holder, attach relevant approvals (e.g. ethics committee opinion).

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.content:
Applicants are required to upload relevant attachments when submitting their application.

The exact list of required documents depends on the purpose of data use, the data holders involved, and national requirements (for example, some countries may require an ethics approval).

The application form will automatically indicate which attachments are needed based on your selected datasets and purpose.

The maximum file size for each attachment is 1 MB, but multiple files can be added.

Uploaded documents will be automatically translated into the required languages to speed up the evaluation process.

fees.title: Fees
fees.p1_before: Health Data Access Bodies (HDABs) and data holders may charge
fees.p1_after: for processing data requests and data access applications, in line with Articles 73 and 74 of the EHDS Regulation.
fees.heading: Fees may cover the following activities:

items.receipt: receipt and completeness check of the application;
items.evaluation: evaluation and decision on the data request or permit;
items.extraction: extraction, preparation, and quality assurance of the datasets;
items.provision: provision of data in anonymised or pseudonymised form within a Secure Processing Environment (SPE);
items.support: maintenance and user support during the authorised project period.

fees.p2_after: before approval and may choose to proceed, revise, or withdraw the application.
fees.p3: Fees apply even if a request is later cancelled or results in a negative decision, limited to costs already incurred.

learnMoreAboutDataAccess.title: Learn more about data access and requests under the European Health Data Space (EHDS)
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.intro: If you need further guidance on how to prepare or evaluate an application for secondary use of health data, the following official TEHDAS2 Guidelines complement the information provided on this page. They are aligned with Chapter IV of Regulation (EU) 2025/327 (EHDS Regulation) and support a consistent implementation across the EU.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_title: Deliverable 5.2 – Guidelines for Health Data Access Bodies on Allowed and Prohibited Purposes
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_p1: Explains which secondary use purposes are authorised under Article 53 of the EHDS Regulation and which uses are prohibited (Article 54).
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_p2: It helps applicants and HDABs ensure that the requested use falls within the legal scope of the EHDS.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_c1: exhaustive list of authorised purposes (public health, research, policy-making, education, innovation, etc.);
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_c2: prohibited purposes such as marketing, discrimination or harmful profiling;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d52_c3: examples illustrating compliant and non-compliant use cases.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.readD52: Read D5.2 – Allowed and Prohibited Purposes {ref}.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d41_title: Deliverable 4.1 – Guidelines for HDABs on Fees and Penalties
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d41_p1: Provides principles for calculating fees for processing data access applications and for establishing penalties in case of non-compliance, in line with Articles 73 and 74 of the EHDS Regulation.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d41_c1: cost-recovery approach for different application types;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d41_c2: transparency and non-discrimination in fee structures;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d41_c3: proportionality of penalties and examples of misuse scenarios.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_title: Deliverable 6.2 – Good Application Practice for Data Access and Data Requests
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_p1: Guides applicants through the preparation of complete, consistent and well-documented applications for secondary use of health data.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_c1: structure and content of the Data Request and Data Access form;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_c2: guidance on attachments, mandatory fields, and supporting documents;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_c3: examples of research, policy and innovation use cases;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d62_c4: practical tips for improving processing time and approval chances.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d63_title: Deliverable 6.3 – Procedures and Formats for Data Access
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d63_p1: Details how HDABs should assess and authorise applications in a harmonised way.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d63_c2: technical, semantic, and legal validation steps;
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d63_c3: principles for the Secure Processing Environment (SPE);
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.d63_c4: checks on data minimisation, necessity and proportionality (Articles 68–70).
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.readD63: Read D6.3 – Procedures and Formats for Data Access {ref}.
learnMoreAboutDataAccess.closing: These guidelines provide detailed explanations and examples that complement the information displayed on this portal. Applicants and HDABs are encouraged to consult them before submitting or evaluating an application.

chooseApplicationPath.title: Choose your application path
chooseApplicationPath.dataProtectionContent:
HDABs prioritise the protection of individual-level data.
Anonymised data are the default option.
Access to pseudonymised data is possible only if essential for the intended purpose of use and duly justified.
Selecting the correct path helps avoid delays or additional review.

request.title: Data Request application
request.subtitle: Choose this path if anonymised or aggregated statistical results are sufficient for your objectives.
request.youWillReceiveItem1: aggregated anonymised outputs generated by the HDAB or trusted data holder;
request.youWillReceiveItem3: results produced under HDAB control and validated for statistical soundness.
request.useCaseItem1: analysing population-level trends or summary statistics (e.g. number of cancer cases in a region);
request.useCaseItem2: querying dataset characteristics (e.g. how many individuals with mutation X are present in dataset D)
request.tipText: You may contact the HDAB beforehand to clarify dataset details before submitting your request.

access.title: Data Access application
access.subtitle: Choose this path if you need individual-level data and aggregated results are not sufficient.
access.youWillAccessItem1: only within an audited Secure Processing Environment (SPE);
access.youWillAccessItem2: in anonymised or, when strictly necessary and justified, pseudonymised form.
access.finePrint1: Applicants must explain why such data are essential and demonstrate compliance with the data minimisation principle.
access.useCaseItem1: linking patient-level data across datasets or Member States (e.g. long-term outcomes of diabetes treatments);
access.useCaseItem2: developing or validating algorithms, AI models, or public health research requiring pseudonymised records.
access.finePrint2: Data access can only be authorised for the purposes listed in Article 53(1) of Regulation (EU) 2025/327 (EHDS Regulation), and cannot be granted for prohibited purposes as defined in Article 54.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.intro: This space provides a comprehensive overview of the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure, the official EU platform enabling the secondary use of health data across borders.
introduction.bullet1: This space provides a comprehensive overview of the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure, the official EU platform enabling the secondary use of health data across borders, as defined in the {ehds}.
introduction.bullet2: A description of the main components and services, including interoperability mechanisms, data access workflows, and security features.
introduction.bullet3: Guidance for Member States, EU bodies and other authorised users on how to connect, exchange metadata, and manage data access applications or data requests.
introduction.bullet4: Details on the open-source modules, technical architecture, and compliance with EU standards such as DCAT Application profile for data portals in Europe (DCAT-AP).
introduction.dcat: DCAT Application profile for data portals in Europe (DCAT-AP)
introduction.audience: Whether you are a policymaker, developer, health data access body, or simply curious about the European health data infrastructure - this page will help you understand how the system works, how to engage with it, and where to go for further technical resources.
introduction.note: This platform is under active development. Contributions are encouraged to help shape the future development.
introduction.ownership: The HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform is developed by the European Commission under the European Health Data Space Regulation. It is open-source and progressively rolled out in close cooperation with Member States and partners.

overview.title: Overview of the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure
overview.para1: The HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure is the official EU digital infrastructure for the secondary use of health data, established under the {ehds}. Operated by the European Commission, it enables secure, cross-border access to health data for research, innovation, policy-making, and regulatory purposes.
overview.list_intro: The infrastructure connects three categories of participants:
overview.bullet1: Member States, each designating a National Contact Point for Secondary Use (NCP-SU), establishing a national health metadata catalogue, and appointing one or more Health Data Access Bodies (HDABs) responsible for managing data access applications and issuing data permits.
overview.bullet2: EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (EUIBs), represented by the Union Health Data Access Service (UHDAS), which fulfils a role equivalent to HDABs for data under EU-level responsibility.
overview.bullet3: Other authorised participants, such as European Research Infrastructure Consortia, European Digital Infrastructure Consortia, third countries, or international organisations, subject to prior approval by the EHDS Board and required to follow the same rules of interoperability and data protection.
overview.para2: At the heart of the infrastructure is the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform, a system operated by the Commission that aggregates metadata from national catalogues into a single EU Dataset Catalogue. It enables a streamlined application process for cross-border or multi-country data access, routing requests to the appropriate national or Union-level access bodies and facilitating transparency and traceability of decisions.

workflow.title: How the HealthData{'@'}EU Infrastructure Works
workflow.intro: The HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure enables secure and structured exchange of metadata and data access applications between authorised actors, using a harmonised, interoperable setup.
workflow.step1: Step 1 – Publishing datasets: Each data holder (e.g. hospital, registry) provides metadata about datasets to the national health data catalogue. These catalogues are synchronised with the EU Dataset Catalogue via the Central Platform.
workflow.step2: Step 2 – Searching for data: A data applicant (e.g. researcher, regulator) uses the Central Platform to search and filter metadata records. Selected datasets are added to a virtual “basket.”
workflow.step3: Step 3 – Submitting an application: The applicant fills in a harmonised application form via the platform and submits it. The form is routed automatically to the relevant National Contact Points for Secondary Use (NCP-SUs) based on the selected datasets.
workflow.step4: Step 4 – Evaluation and response: The NCP-SUs forward the application to the corresponding Health Data Access Bodies (HDABs). Each HDAB evaluates the application and either issues a data permit or provides a reasoned refusal. The decision is sent back to the platform and displayed to the applicant.
workflow.step5: Step 5 – Audit and follow-up: The platform logs all exchanges and supports monitoring and reporting functions, ensuring compliance with the EHDS Regulation and transparency throughout the data lifecycle.
workflow.delivery: All messages, including applications and status updates, are exchanged using the eDelivery Domibus system, following the AS4 protocol. This guarantees interoperability, end-to-end security, and traceability of exchanges across all participating nodes.
workflow.auth: Access to the platform requires an EU Login account. Different roles (e.g. applicant, HDAB, administrator) are defined and managed via a role-based access control system integrated with EU Login and Keycloak.
workflow.permits: The Central Platform implements harmonised templates for data access applications, data permits and data requests, in line with the implementing acts foreseen by the EHDS Regulation. These templates are continuously improved through cooperation with Member States and stakeholders.

development.title: Development of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform
development.paragraph1: The HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform is the core technical component of the EU infrastructure for the secondary use of health data. It is developed by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety (DG SANTE) to implement the European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation.
development.paragraph2: The development of the platform is organised in ten incremental releases (R0 to R9), from September 2023 to December 2026.
development.paragraph3: Since Release 3 (March 2025), the platform is available as open-source software, allowing Member States and authorised participants to reuse and adapt the components according to their national or institutional needs. All source code, documentation, and configuration files are publicly available.
development.paragraph4: To investigate the current functionalities of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform please check the {manual}.

opensource.title: Overview of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform – Open-source
opensource.intro: The HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform – Open-source Release 3 is an open-source interoperability platform issued by DG SANTE, that provides to Member States the foundation services for the exchange of health-related information (metadata) for secondary use.
opensource.bullet1: Cross border messaging: Receiving and sending structured messages via cross border gateway (eDelivery Domibus) between National Contact Points and Central Platform.
opensource.bullet2: Metadata validation: Validation of the structured message with Dataset record against Health DCAT-AP constraint file: This service checks that all incoming datasets meet the Health DCAT-AP standard, ensuring consistency and accuracy, using the Interoperability Test Bed solution.
opensource.bullet3: Dataset catalogue: Creation, search, and display of EU Dataset Catalogue, which follows the first release of the Health DCAT-AP standard (using Piveau open source).
opensource.bullet4: Data Access and Data Request Applications: Manage data access applications by displaying, completing, modifying, and submitting forms (using dynamic and conditional formulars).
opensource.bullet5: Application Status: The system now supports better tracking and management of application statuses between National Contact Points and the EU Dataset Catalogue.
opensource.bullet6: User Identification and Authentication: Users can log in using their EU login credentials, ensuring secure and clear identification (EU Login implementation).
opensource.bullet7: User Authorisation: feature allows the creation of different user roles, with easy tools to manage and update user access.
opensource.footer: The details of the available use cases are available in the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform Open-Source Release 3 {doc}.

messaging.intro: Interoperability is achieved through the {edelivery} Domibus standard, which supports secure, asynchronous messaging using the AS4 protocol. dcat.title: Health DCAT Application Profile
dcat.paragraph1: A key feature of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform is the EU Dataset Catalogue, which allows users to search for health datasets available for secondary use based on structured metadata.
dcat.paragraph2: To ensure standardised and interoperable metadata, the EHDS Regulation empowers the European Commission to adopt an implementing act setting out the minimum elements that data holders must provide when describing datasets. These elements will form the basis of a dedicated Health extension of {dcatap} - the Health DCAT-AP.
dcat.paragraph3: Health DCAT-AP is being developed by DG SANTE, in collaboration with the {semic}, the {pubOffice}, and expert stakeholders. It will be maintained by the European Commission and aligned with the general DCAT-AP framework managed under EU Interoperability Guidelines.
dcat.paragraph4: DG SANTE’s overall work on Health DCAT-AP specifications preparation is a complex task and consists of number of actions, such as:
dcat.bullet1: Work with experts on defining new health specific metadata types.
dcat.bullet2: Establish and manage the governance mechanism for the metadata specification’s maintenance.
dcat.bullet3: Establish the metadata specifications compliant with DG DIGIT guidelines for extensions of DCAT-AP.
dcat.bullet4: Create and maintain the Health DCAT-AP technical specifications, constraint files, controlled vocabularies, and validation tools.
dcat.paragraph5: The first draft of Health DCAT-AP, developed under the {ehds2}, was implemented in Release 3 of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform. Additionally, DG SANTE used the {itb} to create the validation of the structured message with Dataset record against the Health DCAT-AP constraint file. This validator is available to the public {validator}.

applicationProcess.title: Filling in and sending Data Access and Data Request Applications
applicationProcess.intro: The HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform provides a streamlined workflow for submitting applications to access health data across Member States.
applicationProcess.steps_title: Here is how the process works:
applicationProcess.step1: The applicant searches the EU Dataset Catalogue hosted on the platform to identify relevant metadata records. Once selected, these records are added to a virtual "basket."
applicationProcess.step2: After logging in via EU Login, the applicant goes to the basket and selects the type of application to create:
applicationProcess.step2a: Data access application (for obtaining individual level data)
applicationProcess.step2b: Health data request (for requesting aggregated information)
applicationProcess.step3: The platform automatically pre-fills the application form with metadata from the selected datasets. The applicant must complete all mandatory fields across the structured sections of the form.
applicationProcess.step4: Once completed, the application can be submitted in one click to all relevant Member States - i.e., those who published the selected datasets.
applicationProcess.step5: The application is automatically routed to the National Contact Point for Secondary Use (NCP-SU) of each concerned Member State. The NCP-SU forwards it to the competent Health Data Access Body (HDAB).
applicationProcess.step6: The HDAB evaluates the application and issues a decision. The result (approval or refusal) is returned via the same channel: HDAB → NCP-SU → Central Platform.
applicationProcess.step7: The applicant is notified through the platform.
applicationProcess.step8: If the application is approved, a data permit is granted, and the applicant can access the requested data under the conditions specified in the permit.

eligibility.title: Who can apply for access to electronic health data for secondary use
eligibility.paragraph1: According to the EHDS Regulation, Health Data Access Bodies shall only grant access to electronic health data for secondary use to a health data user where the processing of the data by that health data user is necessary for one of the following purposes:
eligibility.a: (a) the public interest in the areas of public or occupational health, such as activities to protect against serious cross-border threats to health, public health surveillance or activities ensuring high levels of quality and safety of healthcare, including patient safety, and of medicinal products or medical devices.
eligibility.b: (b) policy-making and regulatory activities to support public sector bodies or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, including regulatory authorities, in the health or care sector to carry out their tasks defined in their mandates.
eligibility.c: (c) statistics as defined in Article 3, point (1), of Regulation (EU) No 223/2009, such as national, multi-national and Union-level official statistics, related to health or care sectors.
eligibility.d: (d) education or teaching activities in health or care sectors at vocational or higher education level; PE-CONS 76/24 189 LIFE.5 EN.
eligibility.e: (e) scientific research related to health or care sectors that contributes to public health or health technology assessments, or ensures high levels of quality and safety of healthcare, of medicinal products or of medical devices, with the aim of benefiting end-users, such as patients, health professionals and health administrators, including:
eligibility.e1: (i) development and innovation activities for products or services;
eligibility.e2: (ii) training, testing and evaluation of algorithms, including in medical devices, in vitro diagnostic medical devices, AI systems and digital health applications.
eligibility.f: (f) improvement of the delivery of care, of the optimisation of treatment and of the provision of healthcare, based on the electronic health data of other natural persons.

interop.title: European Health Data Space interoperability with other data spaces
interop.paragraph1: As part of the European Strategy for Data, the European Health Data Space (EHDS) is designed to be interoperable with other Common European Data Spaces, enabling secure and reusable data flows across sectors.
interop.paragraph2: This ambition was explored in the SIMPL-Live project led by DG CNECT, which assessed how the {simpl} could support integration across six flagship data spaces:
interop.simpl: Simpl: Cloud-to-edge federations empowering EU data spaces framework
list: Public Procurement Data Space
European Health Data Space (secondary use)
Language Data Space
European Open-Source Cloud Initiative
Destination Earth
Smart Communities Data Space
interop.paragraph3: The study focused on three core aspects:
interop.step1: Identifying common technical and governance requirements across the data spaces.
interop.step2: Defining specific functional and non-functional needs per sector.
interop.step3: Proposing integration strategies for each data space.
interop.paragraph4: Within this analysis, the EHDS was recognised as a pioneer implementation, with a functioning technical infrastructure (the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform) and operational open-source components already in place.
interop.paragraph5: SIMPL is expected to reuse, where appropriate, components developed by EHDS, and to ensure that its future developments remain interoperable with the existing EHDS infrastructure. This approach ensures coherence, avoids duplication of effort, and strengthens the EU’s interoperable data ecosystem.

architecture.title: HealthData{'@'}EU Conceptual Architecture
architecture.paragraph1: The conceptual architecture presents the high-level vision, underpinned by modularity and service orientation. The system is broken into three principal components:
architecture.step1: HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform – The core platform operated by the European Commission.
architecture.step2: HealthData{'@'}EU Infrastructure – The secure message exchange network.
architecture.step3: National Contact Points – National-level systems responsible for interfacing with local data sources and infrastructures.
architecture.descriptionImage: Conceptual Architecture of HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Infrastructure

systemArchitecture.title: HealthData{'@'}EU System Architecture
systemArchitecture.paragraph1: The software architecture is designed as a modular microservices system with RESTful APIs, enabling flexible integration, horizontal scalability, and maintainability.
systemArchitecture.descriptionImage: System Architecture of HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform and Infrastructure

architectureLayers.title: Architecture Layers
architectureLayers.paragraph1: The system architecture consists of six layers:
architectureLayers.layer1: User Layer: encompasses the actors of the platform. Actors can be divided into two categories:
architectureLayers.layer1a: Contact Points exchanging messages with the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform through the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure (eDelivery).
architectureLayers.layer1b: Data users, General Public, and Administrators which use the platform, mainly through its User Interface.
architectureLayers.layer2: Access Layer: comprised of components from both HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform, and the HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure. The Access layer is the entry point into the platform, allowing users to access its functionality. It comprises of a HealthData{'@'}EU National Dispatcher exposing APIs to send structured content (JSON, XML, and/or DCAT-AP), and a reverse proxy (also acting as a Web Server) hosting the UI components of the platform. HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform components are configured to authenticate users against EU Login. Thus, authentication is configured once centrally and not replicated within each of the services of the platform.
architectureLayers.layer2a: Reverse Proxy - The reverse proxy is responsible for proxying the requests to the appropriate components.
architectureLayers.layer2b: User Interface - based on the Piveau-Hub User interface and provides the user with means to access the available user-facing services (e.g. search datasets catalogue records, create data access applications etc) and dashboards related to statistics and Key Performance Indicators.
architectureLayers.layer2c: HealthData{'@'}EU National Dispatcher - provides with APIs for dataset catalogue, dataset catalogue record, data access and permit management actions to be performed via eDelivery Domibus.
architectureLayers.layer2d: eDelivery Domibus (HealthData{'@'}EU infrastructure) - For system actors to interact with the Central Platform, the access point is eDelivery Domibus. AS4 Messages are exchanged between the Access Points (National and Central).
architectureLayers.layer3: Authentication Layer: Combines EU Login (for authentication) and Keycloak (for role-based access control).
architectureLayers.layer4: Services Layer: microservices that encapsulate the implementation of the business logic of the platform. It is further divided into front-facing services that are indirectly accessible by the users of the platform, and back-facing services which enhance or integrate other services. It is the layer where most of the HealthData{'@'}EU Central Platform services reside.
architectureLayers.layer5: Persistence Layer: where HealthData{'@'}EU data is saved in persistence storage leveraging the following databases: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, OpenSearch, Virtuoso, and S3-compatible object storage.
architectureLayers.layer6: Cross-cutting: services are available to all of the above layers for several purposes like, distributed logging and distributed tracing and platform monitoring API.

physicalArchitecture.title: Physical Architecture and Deployment
physicalArchitecture.paragraph1: The Central Platform is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), utilising:
list: VPC architecture with public and private subnets.
Auto Scaling Groups for worker nodes.
RDS for relational databases.
EFS, KMS, ECR, SES, OpenSearch, and DocumentDB for various data services.
physicalArchitecture.paragraph2: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) is used to manage deployment, ensuring consistency, scalability, and reproducibility. Microservices are containerised and deployed through a CI/CD (Continues Integration/Continues Delivery) pipeline using container orchestration tools (likely Kubernetes).

dataModel.title: Data Model
dataModel.paragraph1: The platform uses a three-layer data model:
dataModel.model1: Conceptual Model – High-level representation of key entities like dataset records, data access applications, and permit statuses.
dataModel.model2: Logical Model – Describes data structure in terms of entities, attributes, and relationships using schemas.
dataModel.model3: Physical Model – Maps entities to specific storage technologies (e.g. Virtuoso for RDF triples, MongoDB for documents).
dataModel.paragraph3: These models ensure alignment with standards like DCAT-AP, FAIR principles (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability), and EU-specific metadata profiles.

technicalRequirements.title: Technical Requirements
technicalRequirements.paragraph1: The system meets functional and non-functional requirements spanning performance, usability, security, interoperability, and regulatory compliance.
list: Support for all official EU languages.
Use of open standards (e.g. REST, JSON, RDF, AS4).
Modular design with microservices.
EU Login for authentication and Keycloak (Open Source Identity and Access Management) for authorization.
Web UI compatibility with modern browsers.
Efficient search and filtering capabilities.
Comprehensive metadata validation and version tracking.
Responsive design with multilingual support.
technicalRequirements.paragraph2: The UI must provide tools for viewing, filtering, and managing dataset records and their distributions, submitting applications, and tracking their status.

api.title: API Specification
api.paragraph1: Every aspect of the platform’s functionality is covered by APIs. APIs are grouped by service (e.g., catalogue, search, statistics, data access, upload, dispatcher). Each endpoint includes methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), expected parameters, and response formats.
list: Dataset and catalogue management (CRUD: creation, update, delete).
Application form submission and tracking.
Metadata indexing and querying.
File upload and download.
Statistics reporting in various formats (CSV, XLSX).
Authentication flows and token refresh mechanisms.
Inter-service communication protocols.
api.paragraph3: All APIs follow OpenAPI standards and are designed for secure, scalable, and asynchronous interactions.
